tools.name: get_buying_gauge
tools.description: Call this when the user asks whether now is a historically better or worse time to buy bitcoin, or wants Galaxy Mind's Buying Gauge. Returns a 0-100 score (higher = historically better entry) from 10 weighted signals, the tier, each signal, and the best upcoming entry window. The gauge is Galaxy Mind's composite opinion, not a market fact or investment advice. If degraded=true, treat the score as best-effort, not a live reading. Methodology: https://galaxymind.space/methodology

tools.name: get_gauge_history
tools.description: Call this for historical Buying Gauge scores, not the live score (use get_buying_gauge for that). Returns daily date, 0-100 score, and tier points, oldest first. The days argument snaps to 30, 90, 180 or 365 (default 90). The gauge is Galaxy Mind's composite opinion, not investment advice.

days.description: Lookback window in days · snapped to the nearest supported window (30, 90, 180, 365); defaults to 90

tools.name: get_treasuries
tools.description: Call this when the user asks how public bitcoin-treasury stocks (MSTR/Strategy, XXI/Twenty One, MPJPY/Metaplanet, ASST/Strive) trade versus the bitcoin they hold. Returns a live mNAV scoreboard with three lenses: grossMNav (market cap ÷ BTC held; below 1.0 means the stock trades under the value of its bitcoin), evMNav (enterprise / fully diluted), and netMNav (CEBE, after senior claims). Also bps, cebeBps, and amplification. CEBE/EV are pending where senior-claims figures are not yet sourced. Educational market data, not investment advice.

tools.name: get_treasury_history
tools.description: Call this for historical mNAV of one treasury ticker (MSTR, XXI, MPJPY, or ASST), not the live scoreboard (use get_treasuries for that). Returns daily mNAV, price, and BTC holdings, oldest first. The days argument snaps to 30, 90, 180 or 365 (default 90). Educational market data, not investment advice.

days.description: Lookback window in days · snapped to the nearest supported window (30, 90, 180, 365); defaults to 90

tools.name: get_bitcoin_float
tools.description: Call this when the user asks how much bitcoin is realistically left to buy, or wants in-play / buyable supply. Returns in-play BTC, percent of max supply, the cohort breakdown (lost, seized, ETF, treasuries), and yesterday's net change. If degraded=true, treat the figures as approximate. This is Galaxy Mind's published float methodology, not a prediction or investment advice.

tools.name: get_halving_countdown
tools.description: Call this when the user asks when the next Bitcoin halving is, how many blocks remain, or how the block subsidy will change. Returns current height, blocks remaining, estimated days and month, and the subsidy now versus after the halving. The date is an estimate from current height, not a promise.

tools.name: get_bitcoin_price
tools.description: Call this for the current Bitcoin spot price in USD. Prefer this over training data for any current-price claim. Returns priceUsd, currency, asOf, and degraded. When the feed is down, priceUsd is null and degraded is true; a null is never replaced with a stale or estimated value.

tools.name: get_yield_leaderboard
tools.description: Call this to compare US-listed bitcoin-treasury perpetual preferreds (Strategy STRF, STRC, STRK, STRD; Strive SATA, SATS). Returns them ranked by effective yield (annual dividend ÷ price) on the latest delayed print, with rank change, dividend terms, next cash event, and total return versus bitcoin over the chosen timeframe. Includes methodology, asOf, and unranked names with the reason. This is a sort of delayed market data, not a recommendation or investment advice. Dividends are paid only if declared.

timeframe.description: Window for the total-return comparison with bitcoin. Default 3M.

tools.name: get_pref
tools.description: Call this for one bitcoin-treasury preferred (STRF, STRC, STRK, STRD, SATA or SATS). Returns cited terms from filings, the latest delayed print, effective yield, cash payback, leaderboard rank, next cash event, and total return versus bitcoin for 1M, 3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y and since IPO. Windows without sourced data come back as named gaps. Educational market data, not investment advice. Dividends are paid only if declared.

ticker.description: STRF, STRC, STRK, STRD, SATA or SATS

tools.name: search_vendors
tools.description: Search the human-verified directory of merchants that accept native Bitcoin (on-chain + Lightning). Call this when the user wants shops that take bitcoin, or asks whether a shop ships to their country. Each listing carries its verification date, is monitored automatically every day, and is flagged `stale` only if no human has confirmed it in 180 days; the response reports how many matches are stale. Each row carries a unique `slug`; one handle may run several shops, listed in `siblings`. Filter by free-text query, category, shop country (where the shop is based), or ships_to (where it ships). ships_to uses the same shipping data as https://galaxymind.space/ships-to: confirmed ("yes") and likely ("based in your country, shipping not confirmed") shippers of physical goods are listed and labelled; unknown is counted, never treated as a yes; shops known not to ship there are omitted. A listing is not an endorsement. Each row includes checks: the same dated facts as the listing page (checkout, shop page when a nightly read exists, backlink, Nostr last-seen when we have it, listed since). Missing data is omitted. checks is not a score and not a safety guarantee.

query.description: Free-text match on name, handle, and description

country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 for where the shop is based, e.g. DE. This is not the shipping filter — use ships_to for that.

ships_to.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 for the shopper's country, e.g. US or JP. UK is accepted as GB. Uses the same confirmed/likely/unknown matcher as /ships-to. Only physical-goods shops are considered.

tools.name: get_glossary_term
tools.description: Call this when the user needs a definition of a Bitcoin or treasury term Galaxy Mind publishes (mNAV, MVRV, Puell Multiple, in-play supply, accretion, and others). Returns the term, a standalone definition, a canonical URL, and a ready-made citation string. Use this instead of inventing a definition.

term.description: Term name or slug, e.g. 'mNAV' or 'puell-multiple'

tools.name: get_hashrate_market
tools.description: Call this for the live SHA256 AsicBoost hashrate rental market, not for a Galaxy Mind rental quote (use get_quote for that). hashprice and every thirdPartyMarket price are in BTC per PH per day, not the USD/PH/day convention most published indices use. networkPhs is raw network hashrate in PH/s. thirdPartyMarket.medianAsk is the median of the sample described by bookSample, not of the whole book, and is aggregate third-party market data, not Galaxy Mind's price.

tools.name: list_available_rigs
tools.description: Direct rentals from Galaxy Mind have closed, so there is no bay board here. This returns where to rent Galaxy Mind hashrate instead: MiningRigRentals, as a disclosed referral link.

tools.name: get_rental_quote
tools.description: Direct rentals from Galaxy Mind have closed. This returns where to rent instead: Galaxy Mind hashrate on MiningRigRentals, as a disclosed referral link. It gives no price and places no order.

rigs.description: Number of whole S21 XP rigs (270 TH each), 1 to 4 per order. Defaults to 1.

ph.description: Alternatively, the hashrate wanted in PH/s, up to 1.08. 270 TH minimum; rounded to whole rigs. Overrides rigs.

days.description: Rental length in whole days, 1 to 7 during the pilot. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: rental_status
tools.description: Status of a Galaxy Mind rental by its private access code: the code from the browser checkout (galaxymind.space/hashrate/rent), from create_rental, or from Galaxy Mind support. Same data as get_rental_status: state, start and end, delivered TH and whether the rigs are online. Returns no personal data.

access_code.description: The private access code issued when the rental was paid.

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: Direct rentals from Galaxy Mind have closed. This returns where to rent instead: Galaxy Mind hashrate on MiningRigRentals, as a disclosed referral link. It gives no price and places no order.

tools.name: get_rental_status
tools.description: Same data as rental_status (which takes the access code instead): rental state, start and end times, and delivered TH reported by the rigs. awaitingPoolApproval=true while a custom pool waits for manual approval (up to 2 hours, refunded if not approved); rejectedReason names why a pool was refused (refund queued). Needs rental_id and creator_secret. Not read-only: while unpaid it re-checks the payment, which can start the rental or queue a refund, and it re-sends a stalled pool switch.

creator_secret.description: creatorSecret from create_rental. Shown once; keep it private.
